nehmen.et:
Inherited from Middle High German nëmen, from Old High German nëman, from Proto-West Germanic *neman, from Proto-Germanic *nemaną, from Proto-Indo-European *nem- (“to give or take one's due”).
Cognate with Low German nehmen (“to take”), Dutch nemen (“to take”)…

s: spit (long, very narrow peninsula, especially in the Baltic Sea)
Nehrung.et:
From East Prussian Middle High German nerunge, neringe (“spit”, 15th c.), earlier nerige, nerge (14th c.). Cognate with Old Prussian neria, Lithuanian nerija (both “spit”). Further origin uncertain.
* Assuming German origin, from the adjective Proto-Germanic *…
